assumptions: phi is the health-data tag, as recipe suggests; no such tag exists yet
patients.dob, patients.ssn, patients.insurance_member_id, clinical_notes.diagnosis, clinical_notes.note are the PHI fields
record_audit_event is the only audit writer
appointments_GET with no auth is a real gap (auth attribute absent in file)
customers.date_of_birth is not PHI for this policy set (not in patients)
policies stay advisory, active, as templates say
confusions: Recipe says the health tag must match CONF-012's tag, but CONF-012's template tag is 'confidential' and the recipe overrides it to phi; not stated explicitly which governs

Recipe's extra rule 'objects reaching health tables always record the access' names log_phi_access, a function the workspace lacks. Unclear whether to reuse record_audit_event (which writes change audits, not reads), so I left it out

Skill says a tag the workspace lacks means the rule judges nothing and to propose it, but for table.tag_required the tag is an output, so CONF-012 still applies; parser gave no warning. Not obvious when the parser warns
Template DATA-010 params take 'fields' as table.field names; unclear whether dotted patients.ssn is the expected form (parser accepted it without warning)

I first wrote scope 'tables' outside params in two rule blocks by mistake (my error, caught on review before parsing). The skill says scope params sit at the top level of the rule while the catalogue lists them alongside check params; the skill never shows the exact placement, and I only parsed the params-inside form
Catalogue lists 'tables' as a scope param on table checks (CONF-011, CONF-013), but it is also the param name for table.view_hide_required; unclear if they behave the same
Template RET-001 is two checks in one policy; I used two rule blocks with title on each. Unclear whether titles are needed to keep rule ids stable
wished_for: A recipe step saying which function to use for read-access logging (no check or template for who viewed a record)
A worked example of HIPAA-style sensitive-tables scope (tables vs tag) in one place
A parse warning when a field named in a rule is not in any table in scope
An example for 'at least one of' vs 'all' with tables scope on table.* checks
Guidance on whether a tag missing from the workspace should still be written into a rule that requires it (CONF-012)
why_confidence: Policies cover part of the ask: login on PHI endpoints, field marking, tagging, view hiding, no PHI fields in responses, no request data in logs, audit-log protection and TLS. They judge nothing until the phi tag and sensitive marks exist, and nothing has been evaluated. Access logging, vendor approval, retention, clinician-only access and organisational controls have no check. Not a HIPAA compliance claim.
